findings.title: Alternate numeric hosts bypass metadata SSRF protection
findings.problem: The new validator accepts `http://2852039166`, although the system resolver interprets that numeric host as `169.254.169.254` (verified with AI_NUMERICHOST, without DNS). In web/validation.py:150–171, it misses BLOCKED_HOSTS and falls through the ip_address ValueError branch. An enabled instance passes its unchanged URL through startup.py:153–160 to clients/base.py:29–35 for outbound requests. This defeats the metadata restriction this change explicitly introduces; it does not require DNS rebinding. Full HTTP execution was not tested because httpx is unavailable.

members.title: Metadata-host blocklist can be bypassed with a trailing-dot FQDN or a decimal/octal IPv4 form (pre-existing in the shared helper)
members.problem: validate_arr_url_config (triggarr/web/validation.py:150-171) checks BLOCKED_HOSTS by exact string match. It applies ipaddress.ip_address only to dotted literals. `http://metadata.google.internal./` gives hostname 'metadata.google.internal.' with a trailing dot, which is not in BLOCKED_HOSTS. `http://2852039166/` (169.254.169.254 written as a decimal integer) raises ValueError in ip_address(str) and falls into the 'arbitrary hostname' branch. Both pass the check, and at connect time the resolver or libc can map them to the metadata endpoint. The strict validate_arr_url equally allowed these inputs before this diff, so this is a pre-existing gap and stays under the cap. pending: confirm that httpx/getaddrinfo in the deployed image resolves the decimal-integer host form to 169.254.169.254.
members.why_it_matters: The control this diff adds to config load is meant to block cloud-metadata SSRF, and these forms get around it.
members.fix_hint: normalize the hostname (rstrip('.'), lowercase) before the BLOCKED_HOSTS check, and reject all-digit or hex/octal host forms

members.title: Pre-existing gap: non-canonical IP encodings and FQDN trailing dot get past the metadata/link-local block (SSRF)
members.problem: validate_arr_url_config blocks metadata endpoints by exact hostname match against BLOCKED_HOSTS (triggarr/web/validation.py:150) and by ipaddress.ip_address parsing (validation.py:154). Three kinds of value get through. Decimal or octal IPv4 forms such as `http://2852039166/` and `http://0251.0376.0251.0376/` make ip_address() raise ValueError, which validation.py:167-171 treats as a hostname, yet the OS resolver may still map them to 169.254.169.254. A trailing-dot FQDN such as `http://metadata.google.internal./` also misses the exact-match set. The strict validate_arr_url (validation.py:85-100) has the same gaps and the pre-change load path had no check at all, so this diff adds no new exposure. It is a pre-existing gap and does not weaken the new control. pending: confirm whether httpx/getaddrinfo in the deployed image resolves decimal/octal hosts to the metadata IP.
source_window: Raises ValueError on violation so Pydantic surfaces a ValidationError.
members.why_it_matters: These are the remaining ways around the metadata-IP block that this diff sets out to enforce.
members.fix_hint: Normalize the hostname (strip the trailing dot, and parse numeric-only or octal forms via socket.inet_aton) before the BLOCKED_HOSTS and ip_address checks, in both validators.

members.title: Rejected URL is printed verbatim in the startup traceback and skips the redacting log sink (credential exposure)
members.problem: When a field validator raises ValueError, Pydantic's ValidationError text includes `input_value=<url>`. At startup the error is not caught (triggarr/config.py:345), so the traceback goes to stderr or Docker logs directly rather than through the Loguru redacting sink. A rejected URL that carries userinfo, such as `ftp://user:secret@radarr:7878` or `http://user:pw@0.0.0.0:7878`, would print the credential. The same pattern already exists in reject_apikey_in_url (config.py:65-86); this diff only adds new kinds of rejection that reach it. pending: show that a supported config is likely to put credentials in URL userinfo.
members.why_it_matters: This project's convention is that secrets never reach logs; an uncaught startup traceback is an unredacted channel.
members.fix_hint: Catch ValidationError in ensure_config and log only loc/msg with errors(include_input=False).

findings.title: Stricter URL validator turns previously-loadable configs into an uncaught startup traceback
findings.problem: validate_url_ssrf now runs on every InstanceConfig.url at load time, including disabled instances. It rejects values the old model accepted, for example a URL with no scheme such as `192.168.1.10:7878` or `radarr:7878`. urlparse reads these as scheme '192.168.1.10' or 'radarr', so the check returns 'URL scheme must be http or https'. It also rejects ftp:// URLs and link-local IPs. The startup path is ensure_config -> load_settings -> Settings(**data) (triggarr/config.py:227). Its docstring (triggarr/config.py:345) says pydantic.ValidationError 'continue[s] to propagate uncaught' and treats it as a schema bug. So a config that started fine before this diff now fails with a raw traceback out of asyncio.run, not the friendly logged exit used for TOML corruption (_log_corrupt_config_and_exit). The docstring says rejecting disabled instances is intended, so the rejection is the control working. The defect is the missing user-facing error path for what is now a user-config error and no longer a schema bug. Whether scheme-less URLs are a supported input is not established, so the compatibility question is left as needs_verification.
findings.current_code:
ok, err = validate_arr_url_config(v)
if not ok:
    raise ValueError(err)
return v
findings.fix_hint: catch pydantic.ValidationError in ensure_config and log a friendly message that names the offending instance and field, then sys.exit(1), mirroring _log_corrupt_config_and_exit
findings.why_it_matters: After upgrading, a homelab user with a stale or scheme-less URL on a disabled instance gets a container crash-loop with a traceback and no guidance.

needs_verification.trigger: triggarr.toml containing a disabled instance such as [radarr.Old] url = "192.168.1.10:7878" enabled = false, which loaded fine before this diff
needs_verification.consequence: Startup aborts with an uncaught pydantic.ValidationError traceback, and the daemon crash-loops in Docker until the user hand-edits the TOML
